|archive-date=April 30, 2023}} (born November 5, 1995) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. A {{height|ft=6|in=7}} [[swingman]], Pinson was the starting [[shooting guard]] for the Tar Heels' [[2016–17 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2017 NCAA championship team]]. ==High school career== [[File: 20140402 MCDAAG Theo Pinson.JPG|thumb|left|upright|Pinson in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Born and raised in [[Greensboro, North Carolina]], Pinson first attended [[Oak Ridge Military Academy]] as a freshman, before transferring to [[Wesleyan Christian Academy]] in nearby [[High Point, North Carolina|High Point]], where he was coached by [[Keith Gatlin]] and teammates with future and fellow NBA player [[Harry Giles III]]. He was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] in his senior year.{{cite news|last1=Walker|first1=Edgar|title=Three UNC basketball signees named McDonald's All-Americans|url=http://www.dailytarheel.com/blog/future-heels/2014/01/three-unc-basketball-signees-named-mcdonalds-all-americans|access-date=January 10, 2018|work=[[Daily Tar Heel]]|date=January 29, 2014|archive-date=January 10, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180110234222/http://www.dailytarheel.com/blog/future-heels/2014/01/three-unc-basketball-signees-named-mcdonalds-all-americans|url-status=dead}} In the summer of 2011, Pinson was named to the [[USA Basketball]] U16 team, where he won the gold medal with future Tar Heel teammate [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)|Justin Jackson]].{{cite news|last1=Durham|first1=Andy|title=2011 USA Basketball men's U16 national team finalizes roster: Theo Pinson makes the cut|url=https://www.greensborosports.com/2011/06/13/2011-usa-basketball-mens-u16-national-team-finalizedtheo-pinson-makes-the-cut///|access-date=April 8, 2017|work=GreensboroSports.com|date=June 13, 2011}} ==College career== Pinson's college career was marked by injury early, as he broke the fifth metatarsal bone in his left foot and missed 14 games of his freshman season. His sophomore season was injury free; however, he broke the same bone (fifth metatarsal) in his right foot, causing him to miss the first 16 games of his junior season.{{cite news|last1=Spears|first1=Marc J.|title=Theo Pinson perseveres to celebrate NCAA title with Tar Heels|url=https://andscape.com/features/ncaa-tournament-unc-theo-pinson/#story//|access-date=April 8, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 4, 2017}} While on the court, Pinson's passing, defense and leadership played a key role in the Tar Heels' run to consecutive National Championship Title Games. Pinson was also acknowledged as a positive factor in the locker room for these teams, as he developed a reputation as a prankster in both the locker room and with the media.{{cite news|last1=Auerbach|first1=Nicole|title=Infectious both on and off the court, Theo Pinson charges North Carolina|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/04/02/theo-pinson-north-carolina-personality-on-off-court-national-championship/99961012//|access-date=April 8, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|date=April 2, 2017}}{{cite magazine|last1=Schnell|first1=Lindsay|title=The Tar Heels' X-factor? Theo Pinson, who has stolen the spotlight and the podium in UNC's Final Four run|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/03/30/theo-pinson-uncs-x-factor-and-team-prankster//|access-date=April 8, 2017|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 30, 2016}} During the Tar Heels' 2017 championship run, Pinson's playmaking helped the team defeat [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in the South Regional Final, as his full-court drive and pass set up a game-winning shot by forward [[Luke Maye]].{{cite magazine|last1=Rosenberg|first1=Michael|title=UNC's Luke Maye etches his name in tournament lore with shot to beat Kentucky|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/03/27/north-carolina-kentucky-luke-maye-ncaa-tournament-final-four|access-date=April 8, 2017|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 27, 2017}} As a senior, he averaged 10.3 points, 6.5 rebounds and 5.1 assists in 29.7 minutes per game. ==Professional career== ===Brooklyn Nets (2018–2020)=== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Pinson joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]]. He posted 11.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game in five summer league games. On August 6, 2018, Pinson signed a training camp contract with the Nets,{{cite web|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN THEO PINSON|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/08/06/brooklyn-nets-sign-theo-pinson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 6, 2018|access-date=August 6, 2018}} which was confirmed to be a [[two-way contract]] for the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]]. Under the terms of the deal, he will split time between the Nets and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|last1=Dowd|first1=Tom|title=Brooklyn Nets Training Camp: What to Watch For|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/09/20/brooklyn-nets-training-camp-what-to-watch-for|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=September 21, 2018|access-date=September 19, 2018}}{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Exercise Two-way Player Conversion On Theo Pinson|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/10/11/two-way-player-conversion-on-theo-pinson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 11, 2018|access-date=October 12, 2018}} Pinson made his NBA debut on October 20, 2018, in a 132–112 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]], scoring two points with a rebound and two assists in six and half minutes of play.{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Nash|url=https://www.greensboro.com/sports/pro_sports/theo-pinson-treats-long-island-nets-teammates-to-home-cookin/article_aba590ab-de71-506b-b56a-4c857e3fa21e.html|title=Theo Pinson treats Long Island Nets teammates to home cookin' in Greensboro|work=Greensboro.com|publisher=[[News & Record]]|date=November 30, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}} On April 10, 2019, the Nets converted Pinson's two-way deal to a full NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Theo Pinson|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2019/04/10/brooklyn-nets-sign-theo-pinson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=April 10, 2019|access-date=April 11, 2019}}{{cite web|title=Nets fill 15th roster spot by signing Theo Pinson to standard 15, Pinson made his postseason debut scoring 9 points shooting 3 for 5 from the field and 3 for 4 from 3.{{cite web|title=Embiid leads offensive explosion as 76ers tie series with Nets|url=https://thebrooklyngame.com/game-grades/embiid-leads-offensive-explosion-as-76ers-tie-series-with-nets/|website=TheBrooklynGame.com|date=April 15, 2019|access-date=April 16, 2019}} On July 8, 2019, the Nets re-signed Pinson to a reported two-year contract,{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Re-Sign Theo Pinson|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2019/07/08/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-theo-pinson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 8, 2019|access-date=July 9, 2019}}{{cite web|title=Nets sign Rights, says Yahoo's Smith|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2019/7/6/20684689/nets-renounce-theo-pinson-rights|website=NetsDaily.com|date=July 6, 2019|access-date=July 9, 2019}}{{cite web|title=Nets sign 2019|access-date=July 9, 2019}} In December 2019, Pinson began to see more minutes for the Nets due to an Achilles injury to [[David Nwaba]].{{cite news|title=Nets' Theo Pinson: Re-enters rotation|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-theo-pinson-re-enters-rotation/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=December 30, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2020}} On February 4, 2020, Pinson scored 32 points to go with nine rebounds, three assists and two steals in the G League as the Long Island Nets defeated the [[Wisconsin Herd]] 117–110.{{cite news|title=Nets' Theo Pinson: Catches fire in G League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-theo-pinson-catches-fire-in-g-league/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 5, 2020|access-date=February 6, 2020}} On June 23, Pinson was waived by the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Theo Pinson|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/06/23/brooklyn-nets-waive-theo-pinson|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 23, 2020|access-date=June 23, 2020}} During his two-year tenure with the Nets, Pinson was known for his dance celebrations on the team's bench. {{cite web|title=Nets: A Farewell to Brooklyn Spark Plug Theo Pinson|url=https://nothinbutnets.com/2020/06/25/nets-farewell-theo-pinson/|publisher=Nothin' but Nets|date=June 25, 2020|access-date=June 23, 2026}} ===New York Knicks (2020–2021)=== Three days later after leaving the Brooklyn Nets, on June 26, 2020, Pinson was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Claim Theo Pinson Off Waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/new-york-knicks-claim-theo-pinson-off-waivers|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 26, 2020|access-date=June 26, 2020}} On November 19, 2020, the Knicks announced that they did not exercise the team option on Pinson, making him a free agent.{{cite web|title=Knicks Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-announce-roster-moves|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=November 19, 2020|access-date=November 22, 2020}} On November 29, the Knicks re-signed Pinson to a two-way contract with the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Theo Pinson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-theo-pinson-to-two-way-contract|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=November 29, 2020|access-date=November 29, 2020}} ===Maine Celtics (2021)=== Pinson joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Theo Pinson Playing on the Milwaukee Bucks's NBA Summer League Team |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Theo-Pinson-Milwaukee-Bucks-Summer-League-New-York-Knicks-168836515/ |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=247Sports}} On September 28, 2021, Pinson signed with the [[Boston Celtics]],{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Announce 2021–22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/boston-celtics-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}} but was waived at the end of training camp.{{cite tweet|author=Keith Smith|number=1449501516344266752|title=Official Boston Celtics waivers: Chris Clemons Luke Kornet Garrison Mathews Theo Pinson Boston now has 16 players under contract. 15 standard deals, 1 Two-Way deal. One Two-Way spot remains open for the Celtics.|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 23, he signed with the [[Maine Celtics]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Celtics Acquire Two in Draft, Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/draft-camp-102321/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} Pinson averaged 16.4 points, 4.4 assists, 4.6 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game. ===Dallas Mavericks and Texas Legends (2021–2024)=== On December 20, 2021, Pinson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite news|first=Ross|last=Martin|title=Theo Pinson Signs with the Dallas Mavericks|url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Theo-Pinson-Signs-with-the-Dallas-Mavericks-178837876/|work=247 Sports|date=December 20, 2021|access-date=December 20, 2021}}{{cite Pinson and Marquese Chriss to second 10-day contracts |url=https://www.mavsmoneyball.com/2021/12/31/22861555/dallas-mavericks-theo-pinson-marquese-chriss-second-10-day-contract |website=Mavs Moneyball |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-roster-moves/|access-date=January 10, 2022|publisher=National Basketball Association}} On July 1, 2022, Pinson re-signed with the Mavericks on a one-year deal.{{Cite web |title=Theo Pinson Re-Signs With Mavericks |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/07/theo-pinson-to-re-sign-with-mavericks.html |access-date=July 12, 2022 |website=Hoops Rumors |date=July 2022 |language=en-US}} In the last game of the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]], he recorded his first triple-double in a 117–138 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |title=Theo Pinson records triple double in 2022–23 season finale|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/theo-pinson-records-triple-double-030700297.html|access-date=April 9, 2023|publisher=Yahoo!}} On October 29, 2023, Pinson re-joined the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|first=Britney|last=Wynn|title=LEGENDS DRAFT FOUR, FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-draft-four-finalize-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}} On January 19, 2025, Pinson announced his retirement from professional basketball to focus on his family and broadcasting career.{{cite web|first=Austin|last=Veazey|title=Ex-Maverick, UNC National Champion, Retires From Professional Basketball|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/ex-dallas-mavericks-unc-national-champion-retires-from-professional-basketball-theo-pinson|website=SI.com|date=January 19,
